First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{3x-2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{3(x-2/3)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{(x-2/3)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{2}{3}$ | $4$ | $-5$ |
|  | $↓$ | $\frac{8}{3}$ |
|  | $4$ | $-\frac{7}{3}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-5}{(x-2/3)} & =4-\frac{(7/3)}{(x-2/3)} \\  & =4-\frac{7}{3x-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4x-5}{3x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{3}(4-\frac{7}{3x-2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[4{\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}x-7{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{3x-2}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[4x-\frac{7}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x-2|]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[4(3-1)-\frac{7}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|7|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[8-\frac{7\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{3}] \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-\frac{7}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).\end{aligned}
$$
